newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs easier, focus on demand for new bonds.
newsitem.headline: JGBs easier, focus on demand for new bonds.

text.p: Key June 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures were easier in early trade on Thursday, but there appeared a solid floor at around 126.60.
The market was concerned about how strong investor demand would be for recently launched long-term bonds including the May 2.4 percent 10-year JGBs.
Tokyo Electric Power Co is expected to launch a 10-year straight bond during the day, traders said.
At 0116 GMT, the June stood at 126.63, down from the opening level of 126.75. Wednesday's closing level was 126.60.
Because the Bank of Japan (BOJ) did not announce an outright bond buying operation at 10.10 a.m. (0110 GMT), the June briefly fell as low as 126.55.

There was a vague rumour on Wednesday that the central bank might reduce the amount of its outright bond purchases to put a brake on further falls in long-term yields. The bank currently buys 100 billion yen worth of long-term JGBs twice a month.
The market had expected the BOJ to conduct the second such operation this month some time this week.
The contract opened higher, buoyed by short-covering by dealers who had oversold on Wednesday, traders said. -- Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-8570
